intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (600644) on chromosome 11q23.3. Suzuki et al. (2000) identified PVRL1 (NECTIN1) as the gene responsible for this autosomal recessive syndrome. Sözen et al. (2001) found that heterozygosity for a PVRL1 nonsense mutation was associated with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate (orofacial cleft-7, OFC7), which is included here.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by mutation in the NECTIN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations of PVRL1, encoding a cell-cell adhesion molecule/herpesvirus receptor, in cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The title reports PVRL1 mutations in CLPED. NECTIN1 is the current approved symbol for PVRL1.

checks.claim: The NECTIN1 gene is located on chromosome 11q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: which we identify as PVRL1, encoding nectin-1
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. The location is standard gene nomenclature added by the draft, so it counts as restating the paper.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (2000) identified PVRL1 (NECTIN1) as the gene responsible for cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe positional cloning of the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2), which we identify as PVRL1
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is autosomal recessive.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2)
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the syndrome is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Heterozygosity for a PVRL1 nonsense mutation was associated with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate (orofacial cleft-7, OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly. 'OFC7' is a standard OMIM label added by the draft.

paragraphs.text: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder (Suzuki et al., 2000). Rodini and Richieri-Costa (1990) reported ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, and syndactyly of fingers 2-3, showing that some affected individuals have intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2)
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the syndrome is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Rodini and Richieri-Costa (1990) reported ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, and syndactyly of fingers 2-3.
checks.evidence_quote: presenting ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly of fingers 2-3, accessory nipples, and ear anomalies
checks.explanation: The abstract lists these exact features in the 3 brothers.

checks.claim: Some individuals affected with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome have intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on 3 Brazilian brothers born to normal consanguineous parents (F = 1/16) and presenting ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly of fingers 2-3
checks.explanation: All 3 brothers with the syndrome (called Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome in the paper) had mental retardation, so some affected individuals have intellectual disability.

paragraphs.text: Zlotogora et al. (1987) reported 2 sibs with a syndrome that included cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair, and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes. The older child also had mental retardation.

checks.claim: Zlotogora et al. (1987) reported 2 sibs with a syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Two sibs with a syndrome including cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair, malformed protruding ears, and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes are reported.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports two sibs with a syndrome.

checks.claim: The 2 sibs reported by Zlotogora et al. (1987) had cleft lip and palate.
checks.evidence_quote: Two sibs with a syndrome including cleft lip and palate
checks.explanation: Cleft lip and palate is listed as part of the syndrome in both sibs.

checks.claim: The 2 sibs reported by Zlotogora et al. (1987) had sparse scalp hair.
checks.evidence_quote: Two sibs with a syndrome including cleft lip and palate, sparse scalp hair
checks.explanation: Sparse scalp hair is listed as part of the syndrome.

checks.claim: The 2 sibs reported by Zlotogora et al. (1987) had partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes.
checks.evidence_quote: and partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes are reported.
checks.explanation: Partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes is listed as part of the syndrome.

checks.claim: The older of the 2 sibs reported by Zlotogora et al. (1987) had mental retardation.
checks.evidence_quote: The older child also has mental retardation and pili torti.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the older child had mental retardation.

paragraphs.text: Suzuki et al. (1998) described the disorder as characterized by dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is characterized by dental anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate
checks.explanation: Dental anomalies are listed among the features.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is characterized by hypotrichosis.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate
checks.explanation: Hypotrichosis is listed among the features.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is characterized by onychodysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate
checks.explanation: Onychodysplasia is listed among the features.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is characterized by syndactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate
checks.explanation: Syndactyly is listed among the features.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is characterized by cleft lip/cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessive disorder characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate
checks.explanation: Cleft lip/cleft palate is listed among the features.

paragraphs.text: Yoshida et al. (2015) reported a patient with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia.

checks.claim: Yoshida et al. (2015) reported a patient with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: A 7-year-old Japanese boy, the first child of a consanguineous marriage, showed hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia
checks.explanation: The abstract says the patient had hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia.

checks.claim: The patient reported by Yoshida et al. (2015) had sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair.
checks.evidence_quote: showed hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the patient's hair as sparse, brittle, fine and dry.

checks.claim: The patient reported by Yoshida et al. (2015) had hypodontia.
checks.evidence_quote: showed hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia
checks.explanation: The abstract says the patient had hypodontia.

paragraphs.text: Suzuki et al. (2000) described CLPED1 as autosomal recessive and identified PVRL1 as the responsible gene.

checks.claim: CLPED1 is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner.
checks.evidence_quote: an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2)
checks.explanation: The abstract states that CLPED1 is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (2000) identified PVRL1 as the gene responsible for CLPED1.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe positional cloning of the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2), which we identify as PVRL1
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Suzuki et al. (1998) studied families with the disorder (then called ED4) from Margarita Island. Using an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy, they carried out linkage disequilibrium mapping of the disease gene to chromosome 11q23, and haplotype analysis of the Margarita Island families further localized the gene.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (1998) studied families from Margarita Island with the disorder, then called ED4.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype analysis of four complex Margarita Island ED4 families
checks.explanation: The study analysed Margarita Island families with ED4.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (1998) used an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy.
checks.evidence_quote: We have used an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy to carry out linkage disequilibrium mapping of the ED4 gene to 11q23.
checks.explanation: The paper states this strategy directly.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (1998) mapped the ED4 disease gene to chromosome 11q23 by linkage disequilibrium mapping.
checks.evidence_quote: We have used an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy to carry out linkage disequilibrium mapping of the ED4 gene to 11q23.
checks.explanation: The paper states this mapping directly.

checks.claim: Haplotype analysis of the Margarita Island families further localized the ED4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype analysis of four complex Margarita Island ED4 families localized the ED4 gene to an approximately 1-2-Mb interval spanned by just two YACs.
checks.explanation: Haplotype analysis narrowed the gene's location.

paragraphs.text: By positional cloning, Suzuki et al. (2000) identified PVRL1 as the gene responsible for autosomal recessive CLPED1. PVRL1 encodes nectin-1, an immunoglobulin-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule. Nectin-1 is also the principal cell surface receptor for alpha-herpesviruses.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (2000) identified PVRL1 as the gene responsible for autosomal recessive CLPED1 by positional cloning.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe positional cloning of the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2), which we identify as PVRL1
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly, including the positional-cloning method.

checks.claim: PVRL1 encodes nectin-1, an immunoglobulin-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule.
checks.evidence_quote: PVRL1, encoding nectin-1, an immunoglobulin (Ig)-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Nectin-1 is the principal cell surface receptor for alpha-herpesviruses.
checks.evidence_quote: Nectin-1 is also the principal cell surface receptor for alpha-herpesviruses (HveC; ref. 7)
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Sözen et al. (2001) studied individuals with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate in northern Venezuela. They found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation W185X and nonsyndromic CL/P, which suggests that heterozygous carriers have an increased risk of nonsyndromic orofacial clefting (OFC7).

checks.claim: Sözen et al. (2001) studied individuals with sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate in northern Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The study population was sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P cases in northern Venezuela, and CL/P is defined in the abstract as cleft lip with or without cleft palate.

checks.claim: Sözen et al. (2001) found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation W185X and nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X, results in an autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome on Margarita Island, CLPED1 (ref. 1). Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Heterozygous carriers of the PVRL1 W185X mutation have an increased risk of nonsyndromic orofacial clefting (OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: An increased risk for heterozygous carriers follows directly from the reported significant association. The draft words it as a suggestion, which fits the evidence.

paragraphs.text: Bustos et al. (1991) described an ectodermal dysplasia in families from a relatively isolated and inbred population on Margarita Island, a Caribbean Sea island in northeastern Venezuela.

checks.claim: Bustos et al. (1991) described an ectodermal dysplasia in families from Margarita Island.
checks.evidence_quote: These families were detected in a relatively isolated and inbred population with very small neighbouring communities from a Caribbean Sea island, Margarita Island, in Northeastern Venezuela (Nueva Esparta State).
checks.explanation: The abstract describes ectodermal dysplasia in 7 families from Margarita Island.

checks.claim: The Margarita Island population is relatively isolated and inbred.
checks.evidence_quote: These families were detected in a relatively isolated and inbred population with very small neighbouring communities from a Caribbean Sea island, Margarita Island
checks.explanation: The abstract says the population is relatively isolated and inbred.

checks.claim: Margarita Island is a Caribbean Sea island in northeastern Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: a Caribbean Sea island, Margarita Island, in Northeastern Venezuela (Nueva Esparta State)
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Suzuki et al. (2000) noted the high frequency of CLPED1 on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea.

checks.claim: CLPED1 has a high frequency on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea.
checks.evidence_quote: the high frequency of CLPED1 on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Sözen et al. (2001) found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for a trp185-to-ter (W185X) nonsense mutation in the PVRL1 gene and sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate in northern Venezuela.

checks.claim: The PVRL1 W185X mutation is a trp185-to-ter nonsense mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X
checks.explanation: W185X is a nonsense mutation, and trp185-to-ter is the same change in different notation.

checks.claim: Sözen et al. (2001) found a highly significant association between heterozygosity for the PVRL1 W185X mutation and sporadic, nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate in northern Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.
